title: I Gave 1 Elephant to Stockfish Until I LOSE
summary: Reverse-odds: Fairy-Stockfish (level 8, lichess-style UI) gets king + N Elephants (start 1, +1 per narrator win) on a 10x8 board vs the narrator's army. Elephant = rook + knight compound. He wins vs 1, 2 and 3 elephants by pushing rook-supported outside passed pawns, then loses (mated by two elephants) vs 4 elephants after a retry; he notes the engine eval says 4 elephants is still +6 for him and 5 would be losing.
rules: Elephant (fairy piece): moves and captures like a rook OR a knight (chancellor/marshal).
Board is 10 files x 8 ranks (fairy variant compromise, 'working on a 10 by 8 board').
Engine side: king + N elephants on the back rank, no pawns (frame shows black king + elephants only).
Narrator side: full army incl. knights and bishops and 10 pawns (frame shows knights, bishops, rooks, king and pawns on 10 files); exact extra pieces on the 2 extra files not established.
win_condition: Checkmate the engine; +1 elephant after each win; ends at the first loss (4 elephants in the video).
